I finally decided to organize my country’s military in the totally unlikely event conflict arises. You know, just in case. Feedback is appreciated.

Since Cuba’s military has been divided into three main components historically, I continued with the trend and created a structure that utilizes the active manpower and equipment my country has available at this time. Each army is based in provinces coinciding with its name and each army has specific equipment (air and naval units excluded for now).

Within the three main armies, there are two special units: the Havana Defense Regiment is an armored unit tasked with defending the capital city, and the Guantánamo Frontier Brigade is an infantry unit dedicated to the province of Guantánamo for fairly obvious reasons (cough cough ‘Murica).

Also, the current organization is primarily for territorial defense. In the event that troops are needed overseas, it's likely brigades will simply be diverted from one of the three armies, and a reserve brigade will be formed to take its place at home.

Basic Stats

  • Current Cuban manpower: 49,000 active troops, 39,000 reserves
  • Military spending (as of 2022): $2.7 billion USD; $30,681 per soldier (including reserves); 3% of GDP
  • Recruitment: All men ages 18+ must serve a minimum of 24 months in the armed forces (men attending university only have to serve 12 months); service for women is voluntary

Olin had not slept well. He had taken half a sleeping pill but there was too much on his mind. Between that and the baby crying, he had stayed up till five in the morning. Everything had changed and yet, nothing had changed. All the thoughts were there. Thoughts of changing behaviors and saving his family but thoughts are a weak shield when it came to the cravings.

He tried to fight it off with the tasks of the idle. He played games on his devices and read books, listened to music, watched movies. He did all of it. Yet in the back of his mind like a worm burrowing its way through his defences, he could already feel the power of the radiation flowing through his veins.

Just a little would help me sleep, he thought to himself. Just a touch of it is all that he wanted. But it was never just a touch.

Quietly, while the rest of the family slept, he crept into the garage where the generator pulsed it’s soothing hum of power. Carefully he unscrewed the emitter. The light was beautiful. A brilliant blue glow that could bring tears to the strongest of men.

Kurtis didn’t hesitate, he reached both hands onto the device and immediately he felt the power flow through himself. Every cell in his body woke up with new life. Every stitch of DNA rewritten with a single word, power.

He could of held on to the emitter forever but he was attempting self control. He let go. Quickly he screwed the lid back on and retreated back to the bedroom. Not so much as a minute had passed since his head had landed on his pillow that he was up again and back in front of the generator, both hands again deep in the flow of the emitter,

To his credit, the second time was the last time for that night. He went to sleep and even as the baby cried and cried, he could not be bothered. The power was like ecstasy.

Later on that morning when he did wake up it was with the crushing feeling of a radiationless body. While the negative effects of the radiation were long lasting, the benefits had long been expelled.

“It’s late,” said his wife. “Are you going to work today?”

“Uh yeah,” he said. “What time is it?”

“Almost a quarter till. But if you're going to use the bathroom, you’ll have to wait. Your son is in there again taking all the time in the world.”

“Have you checked his levels,” asked Kurtis.

“What?””

“Did you check his levels today?”

“No, but it’s getting--”

“Do it. Before he leaves the bathroom. Use the kit. I want to know where he is.”

His wife knew better than to ignore a command when Kuris was in one of his moods. She did check their thirteen year old son and then brought Kurtis a change of clothes so that he could shower.

“He’s 1.5 percent higher today than he was yesterday.”

“What,” shouted Kurtis.

In the hallway, Kurtis could hear his son scurrying down the hallway and closing the door to his room. Hiding from the consequences of this latest development.

“How is that even possible,” asked Kurtis from inside the shower. “He went up almost two percent in one day! That’s crazy.”

“He doesn’t do the detox. Says he doesn’t like it. You know how he is.”

Their son had started the year at high risk levels of radiation. Slowly with a lot of detox treatments and proper radiation intake, they had managed to lower that to medium risk and had almost reached normal risk, but their son had gone back to old habits. This latest increase was the last in a steady pattern that had started the month before.

I don’t care what he likes or doesn’t like, you get him doing the treatments tonight while I’m at work. You let him know, no privileges until he gets it under control.

Radiation wasn't poison. The human race had developed to the point where it could harness certain types of radiation to maximize functionality. But abuse of that radiation, since its discovery had been almost immediate. And while people like Kurtis condemned the abuse of it’s use in others, they had seemingly no control of it within themselves.

On the way to work, Kurtis stopped at a mobile emitter and both he and his wife absorbed toxic levels of the rawest form of the radiation.

“I only have enough for three doses,” Kurtis said to his wife. “You take take two, I’ll take one.”

“Don’t be ridiculous Kurtis,” she said. “You know I can get more at home. You’ll be at work all day, you need it.”

Kurtis knew this would be her answer. It always would be. And greedily, he basked in the glow of the radiation until it flowed through his body again. Nothing had changed.
